title: Testing and Verification
subtitle: opa test, schema validation, CI gates, reviews
content:
🧪 The Four Suites (Every Engine)

  • Allow-tests: each permit rule's minimal passing input (opa test, Cedar authorize corpus, OpenFGA check fixtures).
  • Deny-tests: stranger, wrong tenant, private-not-owner, expired MFA — including the verbatim cross-tenant test from Lesson 7.
  • Regression-tests: every incident becomes a named permanent test.
  • Property-tests: unknown roles, missing fields, empty inputs → all deny.
Verification commands per engine (CI-gated) 
# OPA: table-style tests live beside policy (policies/*_test.rego)
# test_admin_full_access, test_analyst_team_write,
# test_analyst_denied_other_tenant, test_stranger_denied_everything
opa test ./policies/ -v --coverage   # CI fails on red OR uncovered rules

# Cedar: validate policy against schema before any deploy
cedar validate --schema schema.cedar --policies policies.cedar

# OpenFGA: replay check fixtures against staging (never only playground)
fga check --store-id $STAGE user:eve viewer document:Q3  # expect false
# OPA: table-style tests live beside policy (policies/*_test.rego) # test_admin_full_access, test_analyst_team_write, # test_analyst_denied_other_tenant, test_stranger_denied_everything opa test ./policies/ -v --coverage # CI fails on red OR uncovered rules # Cedar: validate policy against schema before any deploy cedar validate --schema schema.cedar --policies policies.cedar # OpenFGA: replay check fixtures against staging (never only playground) fga check --store-id $STAGE user:eve viewer document:Q3 # expect false

🚦 CI Gates and Change Review

  • Gate: fmt + tests + coverage + schema-validate on every PR touching policy, tuples, or schemas. Red = no merge.
  • Two-person rule: policy changes need a second approver who replays the decision diff (which requests flip verdict?).
  • Decision-diff previews: run the new bundle against sampled production inputs; list every flipped verdict for the reviewer.
  • AI-generated policy: untrusted input — same gates, plus a human owns the merge.

📊 Coverage Lies to Watch

100% rule coverage with only allow-tests is a green lie. Require deny-coverage (each rule has a failing-twin test) and default-coverage (empty/garbage inputs deny). Pin engine versions in CI — Rego 1.x if/in vs legacy syntax must not drift between laptop and pipeline.

🎮 Try it in the Policy Lab → Toggle default-deny off and watch the property tests go red. Use the controls under the canvas to switch scenarios and watch the verdict change.

questions.question: 100% rule coverage, all tests are allow-cases. What is missing?

options.text: Deny-coverage: failing twins + default-deny property tests

questions.explanation: Allow-only suites cannot catch over-broad rules or fail-open defaults. Every rule needs its deny twin; garbage inputs must deny.

questions.question: What does cedar validate --schema catch before deploy?

options.text: Type/category errors (wrong entity types, illegal action combos)
Whether the policy is stylistically idiomatic

questions.explanation: Schema validation is Cedar's write-time gate — bad policy is rejected, never deployed (Lesson 13).

questions.question: A policy PR flips 3 production requests from deny to allow. Correct handling?

options.text: Decision-diff preview lists them; second approver justifies each flip before merge
Merge silently — flips are always fine
Deploy Friday evening to get it over with

questions.explanation: Verdict flips are the security-relevant diff. Two-person review of flips is the change control auditors expect.

questions.question: Last month's tenant-leak incident is fixed. What makes the fix permanent?

options.text: A named regression test (test_analyst_denied_other_tenant) that lives forever
A Slack message saying it is fixed

questions.explanation: Incidents become tests or they become repeats. Named regression tests are institutional memory that runs on every build.

questions.question: CI uses OPA 1.x but a laptop runs 0.x and a test passes locally, fails in CI. Fix?

options.text: Pin the engine version everywhere (container digest / version file) so syntax and builtins match

questions.explanation: Rego 1.x keywords (if/in) vs legacy syntax is version-sensitive. Pinned versions make local == CI == prod.

questions.question: A diff shows 200 flips, all deny-to-allow for one team. Reading?

options.text: Over-broad new permit scoped to that team — block merge until each flip is justified

questions.explanation: Clustered flips are the signature of an over-scoped rule. Diff review exists to catch exactly this shape.

questions.question: How do you write a regression test for a fixed tenant leak?

options.text: Name it after the incident, use the minimal failing input, keep it permanent
Delete it once the fix ships
File it in an email thread

questions.explanation: Named, minimal, permanent: incidents become tests or they become repeats.

questions.question: OPA 1.x if-keyword syntax fails on a vendored 0.x binary in one region. Prevention?

options.text: Digest-pinned image plus version assertion at boot plus CI matching prod

questions.explanation: Version drift between regions is a split-brain fleet. Pin, assert, and test the matrix you ship.

animation.title: Coverage vs Reality
animation.description: Watch property tests catch what allow-only suites miss
